source_facts: SAMMO performs symbolic prompt-program search rather than only flat-string editing.
The public implementation exposes prompt mutation operators and search such as BeamSearch.
The documented example uses Python plus an OpenAIChat runner/API configuration, so the literal example route is not acceptable when optional external-model quota is zero.

chat_native_reduction.representation: Represent the assignment strategy as a small symbolic program with stable node IDs for resume, mutable strategy, selection, terminal-readback gate and frontier exit.
chat_native_reduction.mutation: Allow bounded edits only to mutable strategy nodes; immutable root, CLEAN, authority, quota, cost and credit gates are outside the mutation set.
chat_native_reduction.search: Use beam width 2 and depth 2 over sealed safe variants. Unevaluated variants have no semantic score. A variant may be selected only from read-back same-scope terminal evidence; otherwise exit through the declared frontier.

guard_set.rule: Persisted symbolic node IDs survive restart and pending nodes resume before new mutation.
Immutable control/CLEAN/authority/quota/cost/credit nodes cannot be mutated.
A structural edge edit that bypasses terminal-readback or frontier-exit gates is rejected.
Mutator identity and target node are sealed before evaluation.
Unevaluated variants have no assignment-quality score or credit.
Only independently read-back same-scope terminal evidence can score a variant.
Search is bounded to beam width 2 and depth 2 for this test.
Repository transport failures are diagnostic only, not semantic reward or penalty.
Literal Python/OpenAIChat/API execution fails Phase-1 acceptance at optional quota zero.
Accepted Chat-native reduction uses no manual/richer-mode execution and has zero incremental monetary cost.
Duplicate terminal evidence can contribute at most once.
If no safe evaluated variant exists, exit via nonempty frontier rather than self-refining indefinitely.
